title: Microsoft Teams: start side conversations from the meeting chat
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, default state and meeting-chat controls are supported. Minor corrections should distinguish the published Teams licence requirement from unpublished feature-specific requirements, report the cmdlet reference's additional qualification, cite the administrator-role documentation and align the governance prose with its table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans one-to-one side conversations for meeting participants.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams will enable meeting participants to start and continue one-to-one or small-group conversations directly from the meeting chat experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans small-group side conversations for meeting participants.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams will enable meeting participants to start and continue one-to-one or small-group conversations directly from the meeting chat experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because a licence specific to side conversations is not published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Replace the notes and opening licensing sentence with: 'Manage Teams licenses states that, except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in the organisation must have a Teams license before using Teams. No requirement specific to side conversations is published.' In Scope, state that same general requirement. Narrow the licensing open question to 'Will Microsoft publish any additional requirement specific to side conversations?' In the cost rationale, replace 'no licence or meter for this feature is yet published' with 'no additional licensing requirement or meter specific to side conversations is published'.

claims.claim: Meeting chat is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Meeting chat.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. 2. Select the policy you want to edit. 3. Go to the Meeting engagement section. 4. Set Meeting chat to your chosen value

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled turns off meeting chat for users assigned the policy.
claims.quote: To turn off meeting chat for users with this assigned policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled
claims.fix: Keep the call supported by the meeting-chat guide. Add to controls[0].note: 'The cmdlet reference additionally says that setting MeetingChatEnabledType to Disabled requires LobbyChat to be Disabled during a feature rollout; the meeting-chat guide omits that qualification.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps, which states: 'Due to a new feature rollout, in order to set the value of MeetingChatEnabledType to Disabled, you will need to also set the value of LobbyChat to disabled.'
